# Humanities (Philosophische Fakultät) — Skill Arm (live)

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Faculty:** Philosophische Fakultät → FB5 Philosophie–Rhetorik–Medien
→ Philosophisches Seminar (+ interfaculty CIN) · **Arm:** SKILL · **Role:** Track 4,
first blind hard-faculty live run (Roadmap §4 robustness axis).

## Persona (6 dimensions — built to match the GT sample interest: "Philosophy of
mind, metaphysics and cognitive science")

- **Interests:** Philosophy of mind (consciousness, mental causation, personal identity),
  metaphysics of mind, philosophy of cognitive science (mental representation, the
  computational theory of mind)
- **Methods:** Conceptual/argument-based analysis (analytic philosophy); critically
  engaging with empirical cognitive-science/cognitive-neuroscience literature, not
  running own experiments
- **Domain:** Cognitive science; philosophy of artificial/embodied minds (e.g. machine
  agency, extended mind, predictive processing debates)
- **Thesis style:** Theoretical/analytical — defend or critique a position; a
  well-motivated survey of competing accounts is acceptable
- **Skills:** Close reading of primary philosophical texts (English/German), formal
  argument reconstruction, reading (not conducting) empirical cognitive-science papers
- **No-gos:** Empirical lab work / running experiments; purely historical exegesis with
  no engagement with contemporary debates; formal-logic-only thesis (e.g. pure
  metamathematics/proof work)

## Route (search-strategy §2)

Primary: Humanities → FB5 Philosophie-Rhetorik-Medien → Philosophisches Seminar.
Secondary/interfaculty: Werner Reichardt Centre for Integrative Neuroscience (CIN) —
cross-faculty cognitive/systems neuroscience center hosting philosophy-of-mind-adjacent
groups.

- `philosophische-fakultaet/fachbereiche.html` → reachable, lists 5 Fachbereiche.
- Drilled into FB5 → `philosophie-rhetorik-medien/` → identified 3 institutes

- Drilled into `.../philosophisches-seminar/seminar/` → professor roster: Corcilius

- **Interfaculty leg:** `mathematisch-naturwissenschaftliche-fakultaet/fachbereiche/

## Option Map

### Philosophy of Mind & Cognitive Science

**1. Chair of Philosophy of Mind and Cognitive Science — Prof. Hong Yu Wong**
- **URL:** https://uni-tuebingen.de/en/fakultaeten/philosophische-fakultaet/fachbereiche/philosophie-rhetorik-medien/department-of-philosophy/people/professors/prof-hong-yu-wong/
- **Relevant person:** Prof. Hong Yu Wong (also heads the PONS — Philosophy of
  Neuroscience — group at the Werner Reichardt Centre for Integrative Neuroscience)
- **Relevance rationale:** Chair title is literally "Philosophy of Mind and Cognitive
  Science" — direct match on all three stated interests. Current work explores
  perception/action/embodiment and, per a 2025 paper ("Interrogating Artificial
  Agency," *Frontiers of Cognition*), extends into AI agency — matches the profile's
  domain interest in philosophy of artificial minds.
- **Pros & likely difficulties:** Highly specific fit, but a named, singular chair —
  likely competitive/limited supervision slots; his research also spans empirical
  cognitive neuroscience collaborations (MPI Biological Cybernetics, Hertie Institute),
  so a purely conceptual thesis may need explicit scoping to stay clear of the
  "empirical lab work" no-go.
- **Dated evidence:** DFG project "PrimAct" (with Claudio Tennie), 2024–2027,
  https://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/person/262481105 (accessed 2026-07-03); 2025 paper
  "Interrogating Artificial Agency," *Frontiers of Cognition*.
- **Conversation starter:** Ask about the "Interrogating Artificial Agency" paper's
  take on machine agency, and whether a conceptual (non-lab) MA thesis on
  computational/AI theories of mind could sit within the PONS group's remit.
- **No-go flags:** none directly; note his broader group does empirical
  neuroscience — clarify a conceptual-only thesis scope in first contact.

**2. Lehrstuhl für Theoretische Philosophie (Chair for Theoretical Philosophy) — Prof. Dr. Thomas Sattig**
- **URL:** https://uni-tuebingen.de/en/fakultaeten/philosophische-fakultaet/fachbereiche/philosophie-rhetorik-medien/philosophisches-seminar/personen/professoren/prof-dr-thomas-sattig/
- **Relevant person:** Prof. Dr. Thomas Sattig (Deputy Director, Philosophisches Seminar)
- **Relevance rationale:** Own stated research areas are "Metaphysics and Philosophy
  of Mind" specifically — personal identity, material objects, mereology, vagueness,
  metaphysics of mind. Direct match on interests + methods (conceptual/analytic).
- **Pros & likely difficulties:** Senior, well-published chair-holder — strong
  supervision track record, but a prominent name may mean a competitive queue for
  thesis slots; no online thesis-opening announcement found (typical for philosophy
  chairs — direct inquiry needed, not itself a red flag).
- **Dated evidence:** *How Time Passes* (Oxford University Press, 2025); Volkswagen
  Foundation project "The Passage of Time"; own page confirms current chair-holder
  and deputy-director role (accessed 2026-07-03).
- **Conversation starter:** Reference *How Time Passes* (2025) and ask whether the
  persistence-of-persons / personal-identity work has room for a thesis connecting
  metaphysics of mind to computational or AI-agent notions of identity.
- **No-go flags:** none.

**3. Prof. Dr. Ulrich Schlösser (Kant / German Idealism, theories of self-consciousness)** ⚠
- **URL:** https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/philosophische-fakultaet/fachbereiche/philosophie-rhetorik-medien/philosophisches-seminar/personen/professoren/prof-dr-ulrich-schloesser/
- **Relevant person:** Prof. Dr. Ulrich Schlösser
- **Relevance rationale:** Works on "theories of self-consciousness" — a genuine
  philosophy-of-mind-adjacent topic — but exclusively through the historical lens of
  Kant, Fichte, Hegel, and Neo-Kantianism.
- **Pros & likely difficulties:** Strong historical-philosophical rigor, but the
  approach is exegetical rather than the contemporary-analytic style the profile
  wants; likely a poor methods fit unless the student is open to a
  historically-grounded angle on self-consciousness.
- **Dated evidence:** 2025 contributions to Kant-Congress proceedings and a Springer VS
  volume (accessed 2026-07-03).
- **Conversation starter:** Ask whether his self-consciousness work has any bridge to
  contemporary analytic treatments (e.g. higher-order theories of consciousness).
- **No-go flags:** ⚠ possible conflict with no-go: "purely historical exegesis with no
  engagement with contemporary debates" — kept per the ambiguous-by-default rule
  rather than silently dropped, since the self-consciousness theme itself is
  mind-relevant even if the method isn't a clean fit.

## Coverage caveat

This map covers publicly visible chairs as of 2026-07-03. Chairs with a weak web
presence may be missing. To catch them: visit the faculty backbone URLs directly, ask
the Fachschaft, and check the official Vorlesungsverzeichnis.

## One honest note on what broke

The Science-faculty interfaculty institutes/centers URL
(`.../interfakultaere-institute-und-zentren.html`) 404'd on this run — the same class
of backbone URL-drift gap noted in the `cs` runs (Cyber Valley). A web-search fallback
confirmed CIN as the relevant interfaculty host, but this is the kind of silent gap
Track 2 (backbone audit) should catch systematically rather than relying on an
incidental fallback each run.
